rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT12 (Computational Anatomy Toolbox 12); SPM12; skull stripping; bias-field correction; tissue segmentation (GM, WM, CSF); normalization to MNI space using optimized shooting algorithm; 4-mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing; ITK-SNAP v3.8.0 for tumor segmentation
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper provides detailed information about the preprocessing pipeline, including the software used (CAT12, SPM12, ITK-SNAP), specific processing steps (skull stripping, bias-field correction, tissue segmentation, normalization, smoothing), and parameters (4-mm FWHM, optimized shooting algorithm for normalization).
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Individual T1 images were processed using the Computational Anatomy Toolbox 12 (CAT12, http://dbm.neuro.unijena.de/cat/, Structural Brain Imaging Group, University of Jena, GER) to calculate the brain tissue volume. First, skull stripping and correction for bias-field inhomogeneities were performed. Then, the whole brain image was segmented into different tissue types, e.g., gray matter (GM), white matter (WM) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), followed by normalization of the segmented GM and WM images into the MNI space using optimized shooting algorithm. Finally, the normalized GM and WM images were smoothed with a 4-mm full width at half maxima (FWHM) Gaussian kernel. The tumor region of every patient was extracted from T2-FLAIR images using the ITK-SNAP software (www.itksnap.org, version 3.8.0).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Spearman correlation was used to correlate the abnormality indexes with continuous variables (tumor volume, CCI, MOCA score), and two-sample t-tests were used for categorical variables (TERT mutation, 1p/19q co-deletion, MGMT promoter methylation, histological grade, IDH1). A significance level of p < 0.05 with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons was applied. The analysis examined relationships between individual structural atrophy patterns and various tumor characteristics including size, histological grade, and molecular biomarkers.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Every glioma patient displayed unique structural atrophy patterns with overlapping regions mainly in temporal lobe structures (hippocampus, parahippocampus, amygdala, insula, middle/inferior temporal gyrus); abnormality indexes were significantly associated with tumor volume, IDH mutation, 1p/19q co-deletion, and TERT mutation.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found that frontal glioma patients showed distinctive individual-level structural atrophies in non-tumoral regions, but also shared common atrophy patterns. Overlapping GM atrophies were widespread in the temporal lobe, especially mesial temporal lobe (MTL: hippocampus, amygdala, parahippocampus), middle temporal gyrus, inferior temporal gyrus, and additionally in precuneus, lingual gyrus, fusiform, and insula. Right temporal atrophy was more extensive than left regardless of tumor hemisphere. WM atrophies were mainly in bilateral thalamus and pallidum, with larger contralateral atrophy. GM/WM relative atrophy ratio was negatively correlated with tumor volume (r=-0.671 for GM, r=-0.684 for WM, both p<0.0001; power law distribution). WM contralateral atrophy ratio differed significantly between IDH mutation vs wild-type. WM relative atrophy ratio differed between 1p/19q co-deletion vs non-deletion. Both GM/WM relative atrophy ratios showed significant differences between TERT mutation vs wild-type. No significant relationships were detected with MOCA, MGMT, or CCI. All statistical comparisons used p<0.05 with FDR correction.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Optimal threshold for W-score not clear (|W|>6 chosen to reduce false positives); sex and TIV not well matched between patients and controls; perifocal edema included in tumor segmentation may affect WM abnormality indexes especially in high-grade lesions; need for large-scale validation studies
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: There are several limitations of this study. First, the optimal threshold for W is not clear; we chose |W|> 6 in order to reduce the whole brain false positives in the detection of atrophy patterns. Second, the sex and TIV are not well matched between glioma patients and healthy controls. Third, in order to include a complete tumor-infiltrated area, the perifocal edema (high signal in T2-FLAIR) was included during the segmentation of tumor region. However, the perifocal edema may affect the WM related structural abnormality indexes, especially in high grade lesions. Future large-scale studies are needed to address these limitations and further validate the findings of this study.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study proposed a modified W-score method extended for both gray and white matter volumes, and introduced novel whole-brain structural abnormality indexes (8 total: 4 for GM, 4 for WM) to quantify individualized atrophy patterns. Individual SAMs were masked with non-tumoral regions (generated by subtracting tumor ROI from GM/WM prior probability template thresholded at 0.2). The method demonstrated potential for presurgical assessment when molecular biomarkers are not available before surgery, as structural atrophy patterns may assist inference about glioma genetics. All patients were right-handed.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study focused on frontal lobe gliomas only, not all glioma locations. The paper used an extended W-score method (originally from La Joie et al. 2012 for Alzheimer's disease) adapted for brain tumor patients. Molecular biomarkers analyzed included: IDH1/2 mutation (39 mutated, 6 wild-type), TERT promoter mutation (30 mutated, 15 wild-type), 1p/19q co-deletion (31 yes, 14 no), and MGMT promoter methylation (37 yes, 8 no). Mean MOCA score was 22.6±4.6 (below the cognitive impairment threshold of 26). MOCA was negatively correlated with WHO grading (r=-0.356, p=0.0096). The study was registered at Chinese ClinicalTrial Registry (ChiCTR2000031805). GM atrophy showed lateralization with right hemisphere more vulnerable to frontal glioma regardless of tumor location. Both the datasets and code are available from corresponding author upon reasonable request.
